---
title: "Put a server behind a reverse proxy"
guide-section: How-to guides
---

dastor doesn't serve TLS or limit how often a client may ask. A reverse proxy in front of it does both.

## Tell dastor the pages are served over HTTPS

Add to the config:

```yaml
https: true
```

The sign-in cookie is then `Secure` with the `__Host-` prefix, though the proxy passes requests on over plain HTTP. Without it, dastor goes by `X-Forwarded-Proto`, which uvicorn trusts only from `127.0.0.1` unless `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` names the proxy.

## Pass the original Host

dastor refuses a change whose `Origin` names another host, so the proxy must pass the `Host` the browser asked for.

## Limit request rates

Limit every path, and `/v1/session` (where keys are tried) most strictly. With nginx:

```nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=dastor:10m rate=20r/s;
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=signin:10m rate=5r/m;

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name das.example.org;
    # ssl_certificate ... ;

    location / {
        limit_req zone=dastor burst=100;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
    }
    location = /v1/session {
        limit_req zone=signin burst=5;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
    }
}
```

## Give the server a host name of its own

Cookies aren't kept to one port, so two dastor servers on one host name sign each other's browsers out. Serve each on its own name.
